name: proto_energetics
description: A transferable energy currency before modern pumping (pre-og-05). An exergonic geochemical drive charges a carrier pool (thioester / acyl-phosphate class) that is discharged for endergonic work under load and bled by hydrolysis, all tracked in a conserved free-energy ledger (input = work + stored + dissipated). Tests whether the system captures environmental free energy into a transferable store, and what fraction becomes stored usable work. drive_free_energy / coupling_efficiency set the arm; coupling->0 or drive below the carrier bond collapses the currency (ablations). Coarse-grained, deterministic reproduction (not a wrapped engine).

drive_free_energy.description: Exergonic geochemical drive ΔG available (kJ/mol); below the carrier bond the drive cannot charge it

coupling_efficiency.description: Fraction of tapped drive free energy coupled into the carrier bond (0 = no coupling ablation)

loss_rate.description: First-order hydrolysis / loss rate of charged carrier (per tick)

load.description: Endergonic work demand as a fraction of the carrier pool per tick

carrier.description: Primitive carrier chemistry (thioester / acyl_phosphate / polyphosphate / reduced_metal)

drive.doc:
The sustained environmental free-energy supply — the vent's geochemical /
redox disequilibrium that an early system could tap. Writes a (optionally
declining) exergonic drive free energy ΔG (kJ/mol) that the currency process
couples to. Steady by default; a decline models the gradient waning so the
store must carry the system through.

_contract.summary: Sustained environmental (geochemical) free-energy supply — an exergonic drive ΔG the proto-energy currency couples to.
_contract.description: Writes drive_free_energy = max(g_floor, g_drive - decline_rate * t), the per-transfer free energy (kJ/mol) available from the vent's redox / geochemical disequilibrium (e.g. FeS-mediated redox, H2/CO2). The currency process can only charge a carrier whose bond this drive can clear — so the drive ΔG sets which carriers are chargeable, not just how fast.

outputs.drive_free_energy: exergonic environmental drive ΔG available this tick (kJ/mol)

assumptions: A controlled environmental supply (not a scripted upgrade of the system).

currency.doc:
A pre-ATP energy currency as explicit free-energy bookkeeping.

A carrier pool (``carrier_pool`` molar, charged fraction tracked internally) is
**charged** by the exergonic drive at ``coupling_efficiency`` — but only if the
drive ΔG can clear the carrier's high-energy bond (a thermodynamic gate, so the
drive axis has a real threshold, not just a rate) — **discharged** to do
endergonic work at a rate set by ``load``, and bled by first-order
**hydrolysis** (``loss_rate``). All flows feed a FREE-ENERGY LEDGER so that

    input free energy = useful work delivered + stored in the pool + dissipated

holds to machine precision every tick (the free-energy-accounting invariant).
Emits the carrier charge/discharge/loss fluxes (World view), the ledger shares
(Mechanism view), and the derived scalars the stage grades on:
``energy_charge_fraction`` (is the currency maintained under load?) and
``energy_stored_work_fraction`` (what fraction of geochemical free energy became
transferable usable work?). Deterministic reduced kinetics; not a wrapped engine.

_contract.summary: Energy-currency bookkeeping: an exergonic drive charges a transferable carrier that is discharged for endergonic work and lost to hydrolysis, under a conserved free-energy ledger.
_contract.description: Coarse-grained, deterministic reduced kinetics (not a wrapped MD/quantum engine). A carrier pool is charged by the environmental drive at coupling_efficiency when the drive ΔG clears the carrier bond (soft thermodynamic gate), discharged to endergonic work under a load at discharge_efficiency, and bled by first-order hydrolysis. Input free energy drawn = charged mol x bond/coupling_efficiency; the uncoupled remainder, the discharge inefficiency and the hydrolysed bonds are dissipated; the rest is useful work or still stored. The ledger residual input-(work+stored+dissipated) is held at machine precision — free-energy accounting is the stage's conservation invariant.

inputs.drive_free_energy: exergonic environmental drive ΔG available to tap (kJ/mol)
inputs.coupling_efficiency: fraction of tapped drive free energy coupled into the carrier bond (dimensionless 0-1)
inputs.load: endergonic work demand as a fraction of the carrier pool per tick (dimensionless)

outputs.energy_charge_fraction: charged fraction of the carrier pool (dimensionless 0-1)
outputs.energy_input: cumulative input free energy drawn from the drive (kJ/liter)
outputs.energy_stored: free energy currently held in the charged pool (kJ/liter)
outputs.energy_stored_work_fraction: fraction of input free energy captured as transferable usable work ((work+stored)/input)

math: J_charge = min(k_charge*free*gate*dt, free);  dG_in = J_charge*bond/eta;  dG_store = J_charge*bond
input = work + stored + dissipated   (free-energy ledger invariant)
assumptions: Coarse-grained deterministic reduced kinetics (reproducible); not a wrapped engine.
A carrier bond of fixed free energy (bond_free_energy); charging needs the drive ΔG to clear it (thermodynamic gate).
Capturing free energy into a transferable store is the transition — not merely a favourable reaction direction.

emitter.doc:
Store historical states in memory.

``subsample`` records only every Nth composite tick (default 1 =
every tick). Use this for long runs or composites with heavy
state (large fields, many agents) to keep RAM bounded — the
saved time-series still reflects the simulation's true cadence
via each row's ``global_time`` field.

``max_len`` optionally bounds ``history`` to the most recent N
recorded rows (a ring buffer): once the cap is reached each new
record drops the oldest. Default ``None`` = unbounded (the
historical behaviour — consumers such as v2ecoli that read the
full ``history`` are unaffected unless they opt in). ``max_len``
counts *recorded* rows (i.e. post-``subsample``).
